title: Harbor brief and strategy check
topics: Operational incident review and reliability targets
summary: Quarter-end leadership update focused on operational reliability, capacity plans for Dedicated/Private customers, and a tight hiring reforecast tied to revised revenue assumptions. Action items assigned for rollout cadence, security attestation updates, and a condensed hiring scorecard.
action_items: Maya Patel | Publish condensed Q4 roadmap (1-pager) | 2027-11-05
Evan Brooks | Run Dedicated capacity soak test and share perf spreadsheet | 2027-11-09
Jenna Ortiz | Confirm Q1 community event dates and low-touch kit | 2027-11-12
Noah Park | Share reforecast model with SLT and people ops | 2027-11-04
Sofia Ramos | Produce hiring triage & bar doc; propose freeze list | 2027-11-03
next_steps: Schedule follow-up with Sales + Solutions to align on Dedicated pilot timelines
Host reliability war-room next Tuesday to close out incident actions
Share security attestation updates for Private customers by EOD Friday
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-01 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Asha, Liam, Maya, Evan, Jenna, Noah, Sofia + open floor (remote)

[00:00] Asha Kapoor: ok hey team, thanks for being on time, um we wanted to do a tight cadence today, two things, one: get alignment on Q4 final priorities, and two: talk through the Dedicated and Private ramp risk. we'll keep it under an hour.

[00:28] Liam Chen: yeah, I'll start with a quick infra status. we saw the last incident on 10/24 was - so root cause was a scheduler race on the batching layer, K V cache ended up not— or the K-V cash, Oh god transcription, the K-V cache GC clobbered entries during a compaction window. we've got a patch deployed last week that limited compactions to lower-prio lanes. latency has stabilized but p50 is still a bit high on long seqs.

[01:02] Evan Brooks: to add, the patch reduced the tail by about 18% in staging, prod is trending similar but we need more soak on Dedicated pools because of different hashing. I'll schedule a soak this week.

[01:20] Maya Patel: from product side, the ask from Sales is clear: customers prioritize predictable latency even if it costs a touch more. that pushes us to recommend Dedicated for a set of mid-market accounts. but we still need the cost story — Redwood Opti...um Redwood Optimize recommendations need to be tightened into a playbook.

[01:48] Jenna Ortiz: DevRel has been hearing the same. community folks keep asking about on-prem guides and quickstarts for the Private offering — they call it 'private VPC' but often mean data residency. I have a draft kit.

[02:05] Noah Park: before we go too deep, quick finance note — our reforecast shows headcount is the largest lever, and with the current bookings cadence we have to be disciplined. I'm going to propose a temporary hiring freeze for non-critical IC roles unless there's a revenue-backed hire.

[02:32] Sofia Ramos: that matches People ops modeling; we'll prep a hiring triage doc and define the critical list.

[02:45] Asha Kapoor: good. let's run through the specific risks on Dedicated/Private. Liam?

[03:05] Liam Chen: main risk one: capacity mismatch — Dedicated customers expect pinned throughput; we don't yet have automated slow-start for canary traffic. risk two: security attestation for Private, the SOC attestation docs are 80% there but we need to update key rotation procedures and KMS integration notes. and third: support SLAs and runbook maturity.

[03:39] Evan Brooks: on the automation side, adding a slow-start flag into the autoscaler is doable but needs one sprint of infra work. it reduces risk of noisy neighbor on the shared infra and makes Dedicated more predictable.

[03:58] Maya Patel: product trade-off is time-to-market vs reliability. we can ship a beta for Dedicated with a strong playbook and restrict access, or wait and build the slow-start. Sales says they'd rather have the beta now for a couple bigger customers.

[04:25] Asha Kapoor: risk appetite check — do we let Sales pilot now and accept manual runbook mitigations, or do we push for the automation? thoughts?

[04:40] Jenna Ortiz: in public conversations we'd be fine with a beta, but in private decks we must be scrupulous about callouts — e.g., "beta with limited SLA, dedicated support". community-facing docs must avoid promising full SLA.

[04:59] Noah Park: financially a controlled pilot makes sense — we can gate revenue recognition on passing the soak. but we need exact pass/fail criteria.

[05:15] Maya Patel: propose criteria: 99.5% p50 under target, 99.0% p95 under target, no critical incident above Sev2 for 72 hours during soak.

[05:32] Evan Brooks: that's reasonable. I'll own the soak test and the perf spreadsheet; I'll share the link in the slack channel and update nightly.

[05:46] Asha Kapoor: great. next topic: hiring. Sofia?

[06:00] Sofia Ramos: Here is the triage approach: freeze new reqs for general ICs, keep go/no-go for revenue generating roles and essential infra/product positions. we'll publish a freeze+exceptions list and a process to apply for exceptions.

[06:20] Asha Kapoor: let's be precise — also we should communicate this transparently to squads: it's not a blanket stop, it's prioritization. we need a 1-pager for all-hands with rationale.

[06:34] Jenna Ortiz: I'll help draft communication and a FAQ for managers.

[06:45] Noah Park: on budget, I'm going to circulate a reforecast model by Friday with scenarios: conservative, baseline, and upside; each maps to hiring allowances.

[07:00] Liam Chen: a quick note on the infra hiring we asked for — we should slot that as 'essential' given the work to harden Dedicated/Private.

[07:15] Maya Patel: agreed, but we still need the bar for those hires high; let's keep them senior to minimize ramp.

[07:28] Asha Kapoor: ok, operations incident review — can we walk through the action list from the Oct incident and status? Evan.

[07:40] Evan Brooks: action list: 1) patch compaction scheduling — done in staging, deployed to prod last week; 2) alerting thresholds tightened for KV eviction — in progress; 3) runbook updates including rollback playbooks — draft ready; 4) post-incident customer comms template — not started.

[08:02] Maya Patel: we need the customer comms template quick — Sales and CSMs are asking for this to use in case pilots see degradation.

[08:12] Jenna Ortiz: I'll pair with Solutions to draft a friendly but factual template; will include timing and mitigation steps.

[08:22] Asha Kapoor: who's owning the runbook finalization?

[08:28] Evan Brooks: I'll own finalizing runbooks; estimate two working days to close drafts if engineers prioritize.

[08:36] Sofia Ramos: we should also capture a postmortem snippet for the all-hands so teams understand the learning and the change in process.

[08:50] Asha Kapoor: yes, short write-up, not the full postmortem. Maya will take the lead on that.

[09:00] Maya Patel: yep, I'll write a <450 word note and circulate for comments.

[09:12] Asha Kapoor: community and GTM — Jenna, what's the plan for Q1 events?

[09:20] Jenna Ortiz: target low-cost, high-signal events: two regional meetups, one partner workshop with a hyperscaler, and a virtual summit cadence. I want to front-load low-touch kits that let smaller customers self-serve.

[09:39] Noah Park: those are marketing spends but could be revenue-accretive. if we keep them low-cost, fine. we need ROI assumptions.

[09:50] Jenna Ortiz: I'll add ROI assumptions to the event plan and highlight lead gen expectations.

[10:00] Asha Kapoor: okay; quick round-robin for open floor items. Liam?

[10:07] Liam Chen: we've got pending kernel updates for the compilation layer that could yield 10-15% token-cost improvements on large contexts. it's low risk. we'd like approval to roll for a small subset.

[10:22] Noah Park: token cost improvement is interesting, but measure the impact on perf SLOs before wide rollout.

[10:30] Evan Brooks: we'll A/B on a traffic slice.

[10:36] Maya Patel: product asks we include the cost/perf delta in the customer playbook so CSMs can reason about tradeoffs with customers.

[11:00] (brief technical chatter and cross-talk about rollout cadence, some people talking over each other)

[11:22] Asha Kapoor: let's recap decisions and owners.

[11:28] Asha Kapoor: Decision 1: run Dedicated pilot now with manual mitigations; pass/fail criteria as Maya proposed. Owner: Evan (soak).

[11:44] Asha Kapoor: Decision 2: temporary hiring freeze except for prioritized infra/product revenue-backed roles. Owner: Sofia + Noah to publish process.

[11:59] Asha Kapoor: Decision 3: finalize SOC/KMS attestation notes for Private and deliver to Sales by Friday. Owner: Liam + Security.

[12:18] Maya Patel: Action items as noted earlier, I'll be consolidating the one-pager.

[12:30] Noah Park: I'll share the reforecast Friday, and set up a short follow-up w/ SLT next Monday.

[12:40] Jenna Ortiz: I'll send the event calendar draft and communications FAQ by next week.

[12:52] Sofia Ramos: hiring triage doc will be published by Wednesday.

[13:05] Evan Brooks: soak test kicks off Wednesday night, I'll post the perf sheet and invite observers.

[13:20] Asha Kapoor: cool — last call: anything else? (pause) ok thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

[13:34] End of recording. Note: transcript contains speaker overlaps and some ASR errors (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache").
